$comment: WHAT EACH SEAM'S OUTPUT IS HELD TO. Every declared seam appears here exactly once. A seam whose output nothing validates is a seam whose bad answer flows onward looking authoritative — the roster stage proved it on 2026-08-25, when a model narrated ('I need to create a valid JSON file. Let me fix the formatting:') instead of answering.
$why: Declared rather than inferred in the test: matching a seam's `produces` string against a schema tag name is a guess — `roster-review` produces `roster-verdict` but its tag is ROSTER_REVIEW, so a name-based map called it unvalidated while it was validated. The link is a fact about the pipeline and belongs in config.

$kinds.artefact: writes a file; the caller parses and contract-checks it
$kinds.none: NOTHING validates this seam's output — a declared gap, see $gapRatchet
$kinds.declared: required keys declared here, taken from the shape the seam PROMPT states; validated by lib/agent-output-schema.js validateDeclaredOutput(seam, parsed)
$kinds.per-story-map: one object keyed by story id, each entry carrying the required keys declared here; the consumer applies an entry per story and skips one whose list keys are empty (lib/handlers/tc-apply-to-prd.py)

$gapRatchet: The `none` list may only SHRINK. Adding a seam with no contract is adding a place a bad answer flows on unchecked.

project-roster-review._why_tag: Judged by validateTaggedOutput against TOOL_ROSTER_REVIEW; the verdict vocabulary is that tool's enum, and the rehearsal stand-in reads it from there.

prompt-review._why: lib/prompt-review.js reads ONE <PROMPT_REVIEW>{falseClaims:[...]}</PROMPT_REVIEW> block out of the reply and installs the prompt UNREVIEWED when it is absent. Declared 'verdict' (bare gate JSON), every prompt of the £0 greenfield harness was installed unreviewed behind a stand-in that satisfied the wrong judge (run 19, 2026-09-14).

roster-review._why_tag: Judged by validateTaggedOutput against TOOL_ROSTER_REVIEW; the verdict vocabulary is that tool's enum, and the rehearsal stand-in reads it from there.

roster-specialiser._why: The delta the engine composes the roster from (lib/project-roster.js composeFromDelta): {agents:{name:{persona,ancestor,kind?,seam?,rationale?}}}. Was 'artefact' while the agent wrote the file itself.

topology-router.checkedBy: lib/llm-call.js callLlmJson — refuses a reply with no JSON

cpa-inference._whyPrefer: contextualize-stories.sh gates on .confidence (block below GATE_BLOCK); the prompt's exemplar states confidence 0.0, and a stand-in that copied it blocked every brownfield story at CPA (£0 brownfield harness runs 1–3, 2026-09-14). The rehearsal's estimate is fully confident — the join is what is rehearsed, not the estimate.
cpa-inference.checkedBy: contextualize-stories.sh reads .confidence, .complexityAdjustment, .adjustedEstimate.*, .riskFlags, .missingKbCoverage, .citedSources, .reasoning from the reply (an unparseable reply is replaced by a zero-confidence one); the shape is stated by cpa-system, the fragment cpa-inference embeds as __SYSTEM_PROMPT__.

agent-failure-analyst._whyDiagnosisOnly: Its consumer, agent-attempt-analyst.sh, records the diagnosis as a KB episode and reads nothing else — the target/patch branches belong to the impl analyst (claude.sh run_failure_analyst), whose contract asks for the prompt exemplar.
agent-failure-analyst._whyShapes: diagnosis is ONE diagnosis, a prose paragraph the KB records as the episode; the rehearsal stand-in read the trailing s as a list and recorded "[]" as the diagnosis of every healing event (2026-09-14). A shape is stated where the key's name misleads.

code-graph-detective._whyList: The detective answers with a JSON ARRAY of fix sites — parseDetectiveFindings (spec-mode-runner.js) matches `[ { … } ]` and reads nothing else; its prompts state the array. The keys below describe one element. A stand-in delivered as a bare object was 'NO parseable JSON' three attempts running (£0 brownfield harness run 2, 2026-09-14).
code-graph-detective._whyShapes: A fix site is a file this codeline HAS: the rehearsal stand-in names the first source file of the story's codeline (by its ecosystem's own source/test convention), never an invented path — CPA blocks a defect whose fix site does not exist, by design (£0 brownfield harness run 1, 2026-09-14).

impl-failure-analyst._whyOverDeclaredLimit: A note within the declared length and opening imperatively is accepted by the deterministic format check and never reaches the LLM reviewer; the rehearsal stand-in exceeds the limit the config declares — the exact shape the reviewer, its rejection and the summarizer rewrite exist for — so that loop executes at £0 (run 28, 2026-09-14).
impl-failure-analyst._whyPrefer: Of the targets the prompt offers, skill is the one whose change goes through the reviewer's summarize-and-resubmit loop (claude.sh run_change_with_reviewer_retry: skill_note, kb_entry, tool_creation); an ac/tc patch reverts on rejection and reaches no summarizer. The rehearsal stand-in takes it so prd-change-summarizer executes at £0.
impl-failure-analyst._whyExemplar: The rehearsal stand-in carries the whole answer the prompt states — target: prd with one ac_patch — so the change reviewer and, on a rejection, the summarizer execute at £0; with diagnosis alone neither ever ran (2026-09-14).
impl-failure-analyst._whyShapes: diagnosis is ONE diagnosis, a prose paragraph the KB records as the episode; the rehearsal stand-in read the trailing s as a list and recorded "[]" as the diagnosis of every healing event (2026-09-14). A shape is stated where the key's name misleads.

tc-writer._why: One object keyed by story id (lib/handlers/tc-apply-to-prd.py): a story whose entry lacks a non-empty facts list is skipped, so an answer of {} applies nothing and the gate reports every test story still missing criteria. Was 'none' — the rehearsal stand-in answered {} and the gate could never pass at £0 (2026-09-13).

kb-synthesizer.checkedBy: lib/kb-synthesizer.js — binds {enforcement, reason} as EPAM_RESPONSE_SCHEMA (additionalProperties false) and validates the enforcement against lib/kb_schema.py; unparseable, declined and unmapped replies are quarantined, never stored
kb-synthesizer._why: Was 'artefact' — a stand-in of {note} was rejected fifteen times by the runner's schema enforcement and the synthesizer recorded no_output (£0 greenfield harness run 29, 2026-09-14). The enforcement's shape is read from the same schema command the synthesizer itself uses; nothing here spells a kind.

$declaredWhy: A seam whose output nothing validates lets a bad answer flow on looking authoritative — the roster-specialiser answered with prose on a paid run and only its artefact check stopped that becoming the identity every downstream agent reads. requiredKeys is the key a CONSUMER cannot proceed without, taken from the shape the seam PROMPT already states, so the contract and the prompt cannot drift. knownKeys is the rest of that shape, reported but not enforced: requiring every optional field would reject valid answers, and the defect being caught is an answer that is not the artefact at all.
